title: Artinian test-diagram lifting from infinitesimal etaleness
statement: Let g : X → S be a scheme morphism, i : Z → S a closed immersion, and J = ker i. Suppose every pullback of g to the closed subscheme cut out by J^(n+1) is etale. For x over Z, every commutative test diagram Spec B → X and Spec B′ → S at x, for a surjection B′ → B of Artinian local rings with kernel of module length one, admits a lift Spec B′ → X commuting with both maps.

source.place: Lemma 0A43, proof of part (1), Artinian test diagrams

proof.text: The spectra of the Artinian local test rings have only their closed points, by IsArtinianRing.isMaximal_of_isPrime and IsLocalRing.eq_maximalIdeal. Evaluate the test square there to see that beta maps its closed point into the support of J. For I = J.comap beta, support_comap implies I.support is the whole test scheme. On global sections, fromSpec_preimage_zeroLocus and zeroLocus_eq_univ_iff show the ideal of I lies in the nilradical. The test ring is Noetherian; transfer this along GammaSpecIso and apply Ideal.FG.isNilpotent_iff_le_nilradical. Equality of ideal sheaves on an affine scheme gives I^(n+1) = bottom. The already-proved source-library Scheme.IdealSheafData.comap_pow identifies this with the pullback of J^(n+1). Its defining closed immersion has zero kernel, hence is an isomorphism by IsClosedImmersion.isIso_iff_ker_eq_bot. Its inverse followed by the second projection constructs the factorization of beta through Z_n.

Construct alpha_n by pullback.lift from alpha and Spec(phi) composed with beta_n; the original square and the factorization equation give the pullback condition. Module.length_eq_one_iff makes ker(phi) a simple module. IsSimpleModule.annihilator_isMaximal and IsLocalRing.eq_maximalIdeal identify its annihilator with the maximal ideal. Since the kernel is proper, it is contained in that annihilator, so Ideal.mul_le gives ker(phi)^2 = bottom. GammaSpecIso_naturality identifies the kernel ideal of Spec(phi) on global sections as the inverse image of ker(phi) along a ring equivalence; Ideal.le_comap_pow and injectivity show its square is zero. Together with IsClosedImmersion.spec_of_surjective, this is IsFirstOrderThickening. Etaleness of pullback.snd gives Flat, LocallyOfFiniteType and the open immersion diagonal by Mathlib instances. Give Spec Bprime the structure map beta_n, and apply the FormallySmooth half of flat_unramified_formally_etale to alpha_n. Compose its lift with pullback.fst. Category associativity, pullback.condition, pullback.lift_fst, and the factorization equation prove the two required triangles.

lean.statement:
theorem artinian_lifting_tests_of_etale_infinitesimal
    {X S Z : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ⟶ S) (i : Z ⟶ S)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] (J : S.IdealSheafData) (hJ : J = i.ker)
    (h_etale : ∀ n : ℕ,
      Etale (pullback.snd g ((J ^ (n + 1)).subschemeι)))
    (x : X) (hx : (g : X → S) x ∈ Set.range (i : Z → S)) :
    ∀ (B' B : Type u) [CommRing B'] [CommRing B]
      [IsArtinianRing B'] [IsArtinianRing B] [IsLocalRing B'] [IsLocalRing B]
      (φ : B' →+* B),
      Function.Surjective φ → Module.length B' ↥(RingHom.ker φ) = 1 →
      ∀ (α : Spec (CommRingCat.of B) ⟶ X) (β : Spec (CommRingCat.of B') ⟶ S),
        α ≫ g = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ) ≫ β →
        α (IsLocalRing.closedPoint B) = x →
        ∃ γ : Spec (CommRingCat.of B') ⟶ X,
          Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ) ≫ γ = α ∧ γ ≫ g = β
